newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA CALLS TENDER FOR 25,000 TONNES SCRAP IRON.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA CALLS TENDER FOR 25,000 TONNES SCRAP IRON.

text.p: Romania's Bursa Maritima Constanta (BMC) maritime and commodities exchange will sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron in a tender this month, the first such offer since Romania has liberalised scrap iron exports.
The scrap came from old rolling stock, a BMC statement said on Friday.
The minimum starting price for a tonne of iron scrap offered in the international tender scheduled for September 25 in the Black Sea port of Constanta had been set at $95, the exchange said.
Bidders have until September 23 to submit offers.

Till mid-1996, Romania applied a full ban on scrap iron exports. But in July, the Balkan country set an export quota for scrap iron of 100,000 tonnes this year with plans to fully liberalise export of the commodity by 1998.
Scrap iron from the shipping sector and rolling stock would make the bulk of those exports, the industry ministry said.

Liberalisation of scrap iron exports is part of Romania's strategy to adapt its legislation to that of the EU internal market, in view of its possible membership. The Balkan country now has an association agreement with the EU.
In 1995, Romania exported to EU countries some 1.0 million tonnes of finished steel products, mainly plate, beams and wire rod, official data show. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
